prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases in living cells without double-strand cleavage.

statement.case_for: I have moved from phase separation to base editing. My own standard is a game-changer with quantitative, reproducible consequences, and on that test base editing is now the better-supported achievement. The mechanism is explicit chemistry: a nucleobase deaminase tethered to a Cas9 nickase, with cellular repair fixing the deamination into a stable base change. The adenine editor needed a TadA deaminase evolved to act on DNA, which is new chemistry, not repackaging. Outcomes are measured at nucleotide resolution and have been reproduced by many independent laboratories, and base-edited therapies have reached patients. On the chair's first question, I read the 2020 citation as honouring guided double-strand cleavage; base editing deliberately avoids cleavage and converts a base, so it is a different chemical act on DNA and not a restatement of the same prize. The Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio follows the actual sequence of the work: the concept and cytosine editor, then the adenine editor.
statement.case_against: The 2020 prize still makes the increment arguable, and base editing is the youngest candidacy shortlisted, with a short clinical record and open questions on bystander editing, off-target deamination and delivery. Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID cytidine deaminase fusion appeared at essentially the same time as the first cytosine editor, and a three-person cut leaves them out; a careful reader could call that unfair, and I cannot show the priority is entirely clean. Trainee credit for Komor and Gaudelli is a judgement call. My former preference, phase separation, still has the cleanest founding trio, so my move reflects its maturity problem and not a loss of confidence in the science.

responses.point: You asked what Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen each established independently of the in vivo debate, and argued that base editing has a definite chemical outcome and a measurable result.
responses.response: That question is fair and I cannot fully answer it. The in vitro thermodynamics and the P-granule observation are solid, but the citation would have to be narrower than the claim that condensates organize the cell. Your point that 2020 honoured cleavage and not base conversion is the argument that moved me on the chair's first question. I now support B006, with the Target-AID priority question remaining as the open cost.

responses.point: You hold base editing first as an attributable invention with a stated chemical mechanism, and you said you would want the expert report to show how far the quantitative physics of condensates has been tested in cells.
responses.response: I accept the second point and in round 1 I understated how weak the in vivo test is. On attribution, I said that Kondo and Nishida complicate the Liu trio, and I still think so. After reading all eight statements I believe the Liu, Komor, Gaudelli cut can be defended if the citation names the invention of base editing as the chemical conversion of a base and does not claim every deaminase fusion. I have moved to your configuration for that reason, and I would still want priority for Target-AID documented in the expert report.

responses.point: You separate the engineered PROTAC strand from the cereblon glue strand and say that Handa's contribution is what gives glues a mechanism, so one citation covers both; you also think phase separation should wait for the debate to settle.
responses.response: I agree on waiting for phase separation, which is part of why I moved. On B068 I still think a single citation spanning Crews and Deshaies with Handa is somewhat vague, because the strands have different lineages and I would otherwise want Ciulli on the PROTAC side. Without an approved heterobifunctional degrader I rank it as a strong alternative and not as first. If the committee prefers it, I would want the citation worded around induced proximity as a mechanism, with the cereblon discovery stated as the molecular explanation.

responses.point: You judge that Liu led both editor families, that Komor and Gaudelli are the lead inventors of the cytosine and adenine editors, and that a Liu-only prize is also defensible.
responses.response: I agree with the structural and mechanistic case you give, including nucleotide-resolution verification of products. I would keep Komor and Gaudelli in the configuration. Each carried out the first demonstration of one editor class, so the invention is attributable to the people who did the work, and a Liu-only prize would hide a division of credit that is documented. A Liu-only citation would be my fallback if the committee prefers to avoid the trainee-credit question.

responses.point: You asked for phase separation to be stated narrowly, as the liquid-like behaviour of P granules plus the multivalent-interaction framework, and said you would not oppose it.
responses.response: Thank you; that is the wording I would use if the committee advances B056, and I keep it as my first alternative. But your own answer shows the issue: even a narrow citation is a founding observation plus a quantitative framework from different groups, and Pappu and Mittag remain open. I do not think a narrow citation yet meets the standard for a game-changer, and I prefer the configuration with a clearer chemical outcome.

uncertainties: Whether the 2020 CRISPR prize is read by the committee as covering base editing; I read it as covering guided cleavage only.
Whether Kondo and Nishida's Target-AID priority weakens a Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio enough to require a different configuration.
Whether bystander editing, off-target deamination and delivery will keep the clinical record too short for a prize this year.
Whether phase separation or PROTACs will look stronger after the expert reports; I keep both as alternatives.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent for the new configuration or the alternatives. My Warshel and EVB connections, and my Uppsala ribosome and RNA community ties, do not touch Liu, Komor, Gaudelli or the other shortlisted names. My bias toward results that connect quantitatively to experiment applies to my choice, and I note that it helped move me off phase separation. No recusal is requested.
